editorial:
Imagine waking up in prison after your buddies left you to rot while they enjoyed the high life. That is exactly where you find Mark Lemmon. He hid a massive stash of diamonds in a sewer before getting caught, and now he is stuck in a cell. Enter Mackenzie, a clever insurance guy who plays a dangerous game by pretending to be a mob boss. He hires three small-time crooks to break Lemmon out, but he is not doing it out of the goodness of his heart. He wants those diamonds. It is a gritty, old-school crime story that feels like a high-stakes game of cat and mouse where nobody can be trusted.

You will love how the tension builds as Lemmon tries to outsmart his new partners. The acting is solid, and the pacing keeps you guessing about who will double-cross whom first. While some of the 70s effects look a bit dated, the plot twists make up for it. If you are into heist movies with a lot of betrayal, you should definitely check this one out.
endingExplained: In the final act, the greed finally catches up with everyone. After Lemmon recovers the diamonds from the sewer, a massive fight breaks out among the partners. Mackenzie's plan to take everything for himself fails when the criminals turn on each other. In a shocking twist, the loot ends up causing more harm than good. Most of the characters end up dead or back in handcuffs, proving that crime does not pay in the end.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves classic crime thrillers and heist stories.
